markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback favors recent, repeated interests over broad associations. This motivates testing a focused history representation, but does not establish that recency improves validation accuracy. (2) Current probes measure training-pair separation across positions. Final-position rank diagnostics would better match next-item recommendation, while remaining distinct from validation HR@10. (3) Compatibility and unmet demand are often unknown. Histories establish interactions; missing specifications, ownership and satisfaction cannot support factual rejection rules.

**Related work.** (1) Original-versus-shuffled history comparisons [1] separate sensitivity to ordering from predictive performance. Preserving the last item gives a useful control for older-order dependence. (2) HRLI@K [2] measures last-item repetition. Because production recommendations exclude seen items, it requires a separate diagnostic ranking and cannot directly measure useful recency. (3) Sampled ranking can disagree with full-catalog ranking [3]. The pinned sampled macro HR@10 must remain the selection objective, with full-catalog behavior treated as supplementary evidence.

### Directions and framework

| Direction | Available evidence | Gap | Proposed response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current-interest modeling | Recent and repeated interactions | Recency may overfit one event | Bounded recent-history residual |
| Behavioral diagnosis | Scores under history edits | Raw margins depend on scale | Paired rank and overlap changes |
| Evidence discipline | Titles, descriptions, timestamps | Specifications may be missing | Explicit unknown states |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality / potential / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder.

1. **Bounded recent-history residual: 4/7/3.** Combine SASRec features with a recency-weighted embedding pool. Originality: simple focused combination, but established ingredients; potential: cheap adaptable hypothesis, but risks redundant signals; difficulty: small model change, but requires predictor synchronization. Related: [1,2].
2. **Matched history-edit probe: 5/7/4.** Compare recent deletions with equal-count random deletions and older-item shuffles. Originality: useful combined controls, but standard interventions; potential: identifies sensitivity, but does not guarantee accuracy gains; difficulty: inference-only, but careful position handling matters. Related: [1].
3. **Frequency-matched rank probe: 3/6/3.** Measure positive-versus-negative wins within training-frequency bins. Originality: task-specific control, but familiar stratification; potential: exposes popularity shortcuts, but cannot establish unbiased relevance; difficulty: lightweight counts, but sparse bins weaken estimates. Related: [3].

### Selected idea: bounded recent-history residual

At 0% progress, prioritize the first idea’s low implementation cost. Let SASRec produce final feature h; pool the last k valid item embeddings with exponential recency weights to obtain r. Score candidates with h + g·LayerNorm(r), using a bounded scalar gate initialized near zero. Train with the baseline objective; compare baseline, gate-only and residual variants under identical seeds and the 200-epoch environment default.

Select checkpoints using only pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve routing, data splits, artifact paths and predictor architecture. Retain the diagnosis interface; add valid sample counts and final-position rank probes, reporting unavailable evidence explicitly.

References: [1](https://github.com/Antondfger/Does-It-Look-Sequential), [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722), [3](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651).

idea.description: Add a bounded recency-weighted item-embedding residual to SASRec’s position-level representation, preserving per-dataset training and routing.
idea.motivation: The qualitative feedback suggests that recent, repeated interactions may identify more specific interests than broad historical affinity. A small residual tests this hypothesis without requiring unavailable ownership, compatibility labels or user traits.
idea.implementation_notes: For each position, pool only valid embeddings at or before that position to avoid future leakage. Use the same causal residual during training and inference, with padding excluded and empty pools mapped to zero. Initialize a sigmoid gate near zero, normalize the pooled vector, and retain the baseline loss initially. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four categories, seeds 0/42, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment override with default 200. Save configuration and weights beneath the trial directory; update the predictor writer to reproduce the architecture. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). view.model remains the trained module; log2feats returns the modified causal features and predict_score uses the trained scoring path. Diagnostics must return metrics and metric_definitions, record valid counts, and distinguish missing measurements from zero. Do not use unavailable metadata fields or infer ownership from interactions. This is a proposal; no training results are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset:
  initialize SASRec and gate_logit = -4
  for each training batch:
    h = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
    for each position t:
      ids = last k nonpadding sequence items at positions <= t
      r[t] = exponentially_weighted_mean(item_emb(ids)); empty => 0
    features = h + sigmoid(gate_logit) * LayerNorm(r)
    loss = baseline_loss(features, positive, negative, valid_positions)
    update all trainable parameters
  evaluate checkpoints using pinned validation protocol
Choose configuration by macro validation HR@10 across all four datasets
Write predictor loading matching configuration, weights and dataset routing

originality.positive: A tightly scoped combination connects qualitative feedback with an explicitly bounded architectural hypothesis.
originality.negative: Recency pooling, residual features and learned gates are established techniques; novelty is limited.

future_potential.positive: The residual provides a cheap foundation for testing when local history contributes beyond SASRec.
future_potential.negative: SASRec may already encode the same signal, and improved recency sensitivity need not improve ranking.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small causal pooling module and gate, using existing embeddings and losses.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding, causal alignment, checkpoint loading and predictor generation must remain consistent.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (RecSys 2024)
contributions: The supplied summary describes comparisons between original and shuffled histories using ranking accuracy and recommendation overlap.
limitations: Shuffle sensitivity alone does not establish that a recent-history residual will improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias (2024)
contributions: The supplied summary describes HRLI@K as a measure of last-observed-item repetition.
limitations: Requires a separate diagnostic ranking when seen items are excluded; repetition is not evidence of useful next-item relevance.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes disagreements between sampled and full-catalog recommendation metrics.
limitations: Does not replace the task’s pinned sampled validation objective or provide complete relevance labels.
